problem: BEV-based navigation systems compress aerial images into semantic graphs, topological maps or road-centric classes, discarding geometric detail and missing diverse traversable regions (footpaths, plazas, trails). Road-extraction and segmentation models also fail out-of-distribution, producing fragmented masks.
motivation: Aerial/BEV images give robots global priors for long-range outdoor navigation, but converting them into executable, dense priors is hard. Image generation foundation models encode spatial layout and navigability priors and generalize broadly, so BEV navigation can be reformulated as image generation.
key_idea: Prompt an image generation model (Gemini) to mark the goal on a BEV map and paint a traversability mask, run A* on the mask, and execute the path using cross-view localization to correct odometry drift.
insight: Generating a full traversability prior and then searching with A* is far more reliable than asking the model to draw the path directly: on CityScale Gemini gets Succ. 0.902 vs Gemini-Direct 0.280, and on OOD Global-Scale 0.766 vs 0.293. Generative models also complete occluded roads, so they beat road-topology extractors OOD (0.766 vs SAMRoad 0.339 / RNGDet++ 0.252), at the cost of lower precision and validity and much slower inference (~30-60 s).
method: Goal localization: mark the robot start with a green star on the BEV map; the image generation model is prompted with the language instruction to draw a green pentagram at the target.

Traversability mask generation: a structured prompt (what to mark walkable / exclude, connectivity, coverage rules) makes Gemini paint a dense yellow mask of walkable areas, bridging gaps such as tree-occluded paths.

A* planning with boundary penalty: A* on the binary mask from start to goal, with a boundary-distance penalty to keep the path near the center; if no path is found, five masks are regenerated concurrently and the first successful one is used.

Cross-view localization: BEV-Patch-PF (no scene-specific fine-tuning) matches RGB-D ground features to BEV features to estimate the global pose at 1 Hz, giving the transform between the map frame and the FAST-LIO2 odometry frame.
Hierarchical execution: look-ahead waypoints on the global path are transformed into the local odometry frame and tracked by the EGO-Planner-style local planner at 10 Hz with 200 Hz odometry.
Real-world BEV construction: orthomosaic built from DJI Neo aerial images via WebODM; thin (2-3 px) lines are prompted for better centerline alignment.

numbers_note: Not a standard embodied-navigation benchmark; the benchmarks are the paper's own image-level road segmentation and path-planning evaluations. Real-world experiments (285 m quadruped run, UAV park) are qualitative only, with no numbers. Splits are labeled 'test' since no official split names are given.
results: Gemini-based prior generation + A* reaches Succ. 0.902 in-domain and 0.766 OOD, clearly beating road-topology extractors OOD (SAMRoad 0.339, RNGDet++ 0.252), though RNGDet++ is better in-domain (0.972). On road segmentation Gemini has the best balance of precision and recall but SAM 3.1 is faster and more precise. The system completes a 285 m outdoor quadruped run and UAV/quadruped park navigation using only a conventional local planner.
limitations: Lightweight geometric local planner has no semantics, so small BEV path errors or localization drift cause execution deviations
Relies on accurate georeferenced orthomosaics and cross-view localization; outdated or misaligned aerial priors limit deployment
Generative models may hallucinate paths, are slow (30-90 s per image) and cost API calls; real-world evaluation is qualitative only
